annotation.title_clean: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights: Making Automated Systems Work for the American People
annotation.title_en: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights: Making Automated Systems Work for the American People
annotation.authors_or_issuer: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
annotation.summary_en: Non-binding White House OSTP white paper setting out five principles for automated systems: safe and effective systems, algorithmic discrimination protections, data privacy, notice and explanation, and human alternatives and fallback. A technical companion gives expectations and practice examples. It is sector-agnostic and has no robotics-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Five principles: safe and effective systems; algorithmic discrimination protections; data privacy; notice and explanation; human alternatives, consideration and fallback.
Systems should have pre-deployment testing, risk mitigation, ongoing monitoring, and independent evaluation.
Algorithmic impact assessments and disparity testing should be performed and made public where possible.
Framework is non-binding and creates no legal rights; it applies to automated systems that affect rights, opportunities or access.
Technical companion offers practical steps and examples, e.g. EO 13960 and the NIST AI RMF.
